story.title: Anthropic Researcher Warns of AI Threat to Humanity
story.summary: A researcher from Anthropic has stated there is more than a 10% chance that artificial intelligence could lead to human extinction within the next decade. This warning follows the resignation of a colleague who expressed similar concerns about the rapid development of superintelligent AI that may surpass human control. Experts emphasize the seriousness of these risks, given their access to unreleased AI systems.

explore_lenses.label: Why is the warning about future AI, not today?
explore_lenses.title: The concern centers on a capability jump
explore_lenses.summary: The researchers are not alleging that current public AI systems can cause human extinction. Their concern is that increasingly capable systems could eventually improve their own capabilities and become harder to supervise or contain.

claims.text: Evan Hubinger said the risk from present models is low and identified the feared pathway as superintelligence emerging through recursive self-improvement.
Forecast — Hubinger estimated a greater than 10% chance that AI could kill all humans within the next decade; this is his personal probability judgment, not an established scientific forecast.
Anthropic's April risk report said its Mythos Preview was highly capable on some specialist tasks but not fully reliable, and assessed its ability to perform complex covert tasks reliably as limited.

Whether recursive self-improvement will produce a system with durable harmful goals, or whether it can be reliably controlled, remains unresolved; Anthropic's report says evidence from prior models may not generalize cleanly after a large capability increase.

explore_lenses.label: Does Anthropic's safety work answer the criticism?
explore_lenses.title: Safeguards exist, but critics say alignment is unsolved
explore_lenses.summary: Anthropic says it limits access to its most capable cyber- and biology-focused model and uses technical safeguards. Coxon and Hubinger argue that these measures do not amount to a demonstrated solution for controlling a future superintelligent system.

claims.text: Anthropic says Mythos 5.1 is restricted to vetted organizations, while its more broadly available counterpart uses safeguards that limit risky cybersecurity and biology capabilities.

Anthropic says its system cards document model capabilities, safety evaluations, and deployment decisions; its April risk assessment separately evaluated whether a model might attempt harm and whether monitoring and security could prevent success.

Jacob Coxon argues that Anthropic and OpenAI are acting irresponsibly by racing toward self-improving superintelligence; Hubinger said Anthropic is trying its best but lacks a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence.

Anthropic's own report says that a lack of warning signs from earlier models is only partial reassurance, because a more capable model could differ materially and some forms of concealed misalignment cannot be definitively ruled out.

explore_lenses.label: What could happen next after the resignation?
explore_lenses.title: Pressure may shift toward external oversight
explore_lenses.summary: The resignation has intensified calls for AI labs to slow or condition further development and for governments to create stronger oversight. No single response is settled, and proposals range from lab-level testing and access controls to international coordination.

claims.text: Coxon called for different conditions before pursuing what he described as the industry's 'endgame,' arguing that attempts to rapidly solve alignment should require extraordinary confidence that safer alternatives do not exist.
Anthropic has continued to publish new model releases and safety materials: on September 1, 2026, it announced Mythos 5.1, whose access it says remains limited to vetted organizations.

Forecast — Sky News reported that Darren Jones called for a multinational AI treaty and for the issue to be raised at future G7 and G20 meetings; whether those requests result in negotiations or binding rules is unknown.

The immediate regulatory outcome is uncertain: the supplied reporting describes proposals for stronger oversight, but does not establish that a new treaty, law, or coordinated international testing regime has been adopted.

story_report.summary: Anthropic researcher Evan Hubinger said he believes there is a greater than 10% chance that artificial intelligence could kill all humans within the next decade, a personal forecast rather than an established scientific probability. The warning has drawn added attention after colleague Jacob Coxon resigned over fears that companies are pursuing out-of-control AI. The developments have sharpened a dispute over whether rapid advances toward superintelligent systems can be made safe enough to deploy.

sections.heading: Hubinger’s Superintelligence Risk Scenario
sections.body: Hubinger said the danger does not stem primarily from present AI models, which he described as low risk. Instead, he identified a pathway in which recursive self-improvement produces superintelligence that exceeds human control. Anthropic’s April risk report said its Mythos Preview showed strong performance on some specialist tasks but was not fully reliable, and that its ability to carry out complex covert tasks reliably was limited.

sections.heading: Coxon Challenges Industry AI Race
sections.body: Coxon argues that Anthropic and OpenAI are acting irresponsibly by racing toward self-improving superintelligence. He called for stricter conditions before pursuing what he termed the industry’s “endgame,” including extraordinary confidence that safer alternatives do not exist. Hubinger, while saying Anthropic is trying its best, said the company does not have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence.

sections.heading: Anthropic Safeguards and Regulatory Proposals
sections.body: Anthropic says Mythos 5.1 is limited to vetted organizations, while a more broadly available counterpart includes safeguards limiting risky cybersecurity and biology capabilities. The company says its system cards document capabilities, safety evaluations and deployment decisions, and its risk assessment examined both a model’s potential to attempt harm and whether monitoring and security could stop it. Separately, Sky News reported that Darren Jones called for a multinational AI treaty and discussion at future G7 and G20 meetings.

unresolved.text: Hubinger’s extinction estimate is not a measured probability: it rests on contested assumptions about future AI capabilities, behavior, resource access and safeguard effectiveness. Whether recursive self-improvement would create durable harmful goals, and whether such systems could be reliably controlled, remains unresolved.

It is unclear whether Coxon’s resignation will alter Anthropic’s development plans, other companies’ practices or government policy. The supplied reporting also does not establish that a proposed treaty, law or coordinated international testing regime has been adopted.

related_stories.title: Lindsay Clancy Trial Ends in Mistrial Due to Jury Deadlock
related_stories.summary: The trial of Lindsay Clancy resulted in a mistrial as the jury could not reach a unanimous verdict. A holdout juror expressed reasonable doubt but stated he would not acquit Clancy. Other jurors described frustration during deliberations, revealing that some initially leaned towards a guilty verdict. Clancy's attorney plans to file a motion to dismiss the case following the mistrial.
